valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (CY2027E adjusted diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date, anchored to CY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $18.00-$18.60 and post-FedEx Freight spin-off margin and buyback trajectory)

bear.driver: Parcel volume softness and slower Network 2.0 cost-saving realization compress margins

base.driver: Mid-single-digit revenue growth, ~12% earnings growth from DRIVE/Network 2.0 savings, and $2B+ buybacks

bull.driver: Stronger parcel yield, faster Network 2.0 margin expansion, and accelerated share repurchases

valuation.implied_by_close: At base CY2027E EPS of $20.65, the $324.14 close implies 15.7x; a $370-$377 consensus target implies 17.9x-18.3x at base EPS or $22.42-$22.85 EPS at 16.5x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $20.65 (6.4 pp)
valuation.watch_metric: Adjusted operating income margin and Network 2.0 / DRIVE cost savings realization
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 CY2026 earnings release scheduled for February 2, 2027

analyst_notes: Following FedEx's October 28, 2026 earnings release (which raised CY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $18.00-$18.60), HSBC upgraded FDX to Buy ($370) and J.P. Morgan ($400) and Citigroup ($374) nudged targets higher, while BofA cut to $359 pre-release. Most named Buy targets cluster around $359-$400 (implying +11% to +23% upside vs. our +5.2% base case), reflecting higher multiple or EPS assumptions on Network 2.0 execution, whereas Morgan Stanley remains a notable outlier at Underweight/$160.
